cohort: The study cohort comprises women who gave birth in Peru in the five years preceding the 2009 (n = 10,289) and 2018 (n = 23,077) Demographic and Family Health Surveys.
finding: Cesarean birth rates in Peru increased by 60% between 2009 and 2018, with persistent pro-wealthy and geographic inequalities.
mod_finding: Cesarean birth rates increased significantly in Peru, with women living in urban and coastal regions, those with higher education, and those in the richest wealth quintiles exhibiting the highest rates of cesarean birth.
cross-section timing: Data was collected for 2009 and 2018, using births registered in the five years preceding each survey execution.
